approach_logistics.trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: Park at the Dingford Creek Trailhead, where Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FS Road 56) is gated to vehicles - high-clearance is strongly recommended for the potholed last miles - then walk or bike about 7.5 mi of closed road to the old Dutch Miller Gap Trailhead at its end.

road.name: Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FS Road 56) to the Dingford Creek Trailhead gate
road.driveNote: From North Bend/I-90 Exit 34, follow 468th Ave SE 0.6 mi to FS Road 56, then continue ~12 mi to a fork and ~5 more mi to the vehicle gate at Dingford Creek Trailhead; the road beyond is closed to vehicles. Notoriously rough and pothole-scarred past Garfield Ledges — high-clearance vehicles recommended.

road.driveNote: From I-90 take Exit 52, turn north across the freeway overpass, then into the large paved PCT North Trailhead (Pacific Crest Trail 2000) parking lot; a day-use fee applies.

approach_logistics.trailhead: North Fork Skykomish Trailhead (Quartz Creek Trail #1050)
approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the North Fork Skykomish Trailhead at the end of FR 63, reached from US-2 at Skykomish via Beckler Road (FR 65) over Jack Pass

road.name: Beckler Road (FR 65) over Jack Pass to the North Fork Skykomish Road (FR 63)
road.driveNote: From US-2 just east of Skykomish, turn north on Beckler Road (FR 65) and follow it about 15 miles over Jack Pass, then turn right on FR 63 and drive 4.2 miles to its end at the North Fork Skykomish Trailhead, where the Quartz Creek trail starts. Rough gravel; high clearance recommended. Both this road and the Index-Galena Road along the North Fork Skykomish have been closed by washouts and storm damage in recent years, so check road status before driving.

approach_variants.name: Quartz Creek Trail over Curry Gap and the Pride Glacier
approach_variants.notes: This is a different trailhead from the peak's scramble route — do not stop at the Blanca Lake trailhead. Drive on to the end of FR 63, begin at the North Fork Skykomish trailhead, and follow the Quartz Creek trail about four miles to Curry Gap, at the junction with the Bald Eagle Mountain trail. From the gap, head west and southwest along an up-and-down ridge toward the peak, leaving the ridge where the ground allows to cross the glacier west-northwest toward the cliffs below the neighbouring summit. The route-finding hazard on this leg is the cliff bands in the basin, not the glacier.
approach_variants.season: June to September; spring ski ascents and descents of this side are also recorded.
hazards: Crevasse-fall hazard on the glacier crossing
Cliff-band route-finding in the basin between the gap and the glacier
Rockfall on the third-class band above the glacier
The up-and-down ridge between the gap and the glacier is longer in practice than it looks on a map
approach_variants.baseFinding: The base of the climbing is where the glacier meets rock on the peak's northeast side, at about six thousand feet, and the physical test is which hand the ice is on. The line climbs third-class rock along the climber's-left edge of the glacier, so once you are on rock the ice should stay on your right the whole way up to the summit's southeast corner. If the ice is on your left, you have crossed to the wrong edge. The second confirmation is what you passed: the cliffs below the neighbouring summit are an aiming mark on the crossing, not the objective — you traverse beneath them and then turn up onto rock. Negative markers: if you are still on low-angle ice with cliffs directly overhead and the summit well off to one side, you are under the neighbouring peak rather than this one; if you have come up a faint climbers' path from a small lake with a subsidiary point beside you, you are on the south-ridge scramble from the other side of the mountain.

why: Quartz Creek Trail #1050 starts at the North Fork Skykomish Trailhead at the end of FR 63 (via Beckler Road FR 65 / Jack Pass, Skykomish Ranger District), as the row's own approach prose says; name, road and variant note wrongly put it on the North Fork Sauk / Darrington side. Coordinates are the Forest Service's stated trailhead location.
waypointNote: No Trailhead waypoint exists (only the summit). Also access.landManager names the Darrington Ranger District; the trailhead is on the Skykomish Ranger District (the peak itself straddles the boundary) - left unpatched. The Blanca Lake sibling records a 2026 closure of FR 65 beyond Jack Pass and FR 63 from the FR 65 side; road.status was null and is left null rather than asserting this route's current state.

patch.approach: Mount Formidable is a deep objective on the Ptarmigan Traverse, reached from the Cascade Pass Trailhead at the end of the Cascade River Road. Take the maintained trail to Cascade Pass, then leave it and work across the Mixup flank on boot path, talus and snow, up the Cache Glacier to Cache Col, and down the far side to camp at Kool-Aid Lake. From the lake continue south past Art's Knoll and cross the Red Ledge, then follow a rough path over meadow, snow and talus and drop several hundred feet to the bench on the Middle Cascade Glacier between its two icefalls. Cross the bench to the foot of the Formidable Glacier below the northeast face. Allow a full day or more from the car to Kool-Aid Lake and about three hours from camp to the base of the face. The South Route from Yang Yang Lakes is the descent, not the approach. This is a multi-day glaciated objective that needs glacier travel skills.

road.name: Cascade River Road (Forest Road 15)
road.status: Paved to about mile 10, then gravel with potholes and washboard to its end at mile 22.3 (Cascade Pass Trailhead, 3,600 ft).
road.driveNote: Roughly 3.5-4 hours from Seattle via SR-20 to Marblemount, then the Cascade River Road to the Cascade Pass Trailhead at its end, followed by a long wilderness approach. No RVs, large trailers, or vehicles over 22 feet on the upper gravel section.
road.seasonalGate: Closed by snow in winter, historically near Eldorado Creek around milepost 20; the road reopens to the trailhead as snowmelt and repairs allow, typically over late spring and early summer.

why: Approach prose described the South Route via Yang Yang Lakes (this route's descent) instead of the Red Ledge / Middle Cascade Glacier bench approach to the Formidable Glacier that the row's own variant, timing (start from Kool-Aid Lake) and trip reports describe; road led with Stehekin though the trailhead is Cascade Pass. Road name/status copied from the South Face sibling; seasonalGate kept.
waypointNote: Only Trailhead and Summit waypoints; both fine.

road.name: WA-20 (North Cascades Highway) to the hairpin pullout below Washington Pass
road.driveNote: From the east (Mazama/Winthrop) or west via Highway 20 to the big 180-degree hairpin turn just east of Washington Pass; park at the pullout there, at the bottom of Spire Gully.
road.seasonalGate: Washington Pass closed in winter (typically late fall to spring)

why: driveNote sent drivers to the Blue Lake Trailhead while road.name, trailhead, pin and approach all start at the SR-20 hairpin pullout east of Washington Pass (Spire Gully); wording follows the row's own hairpin waypoint.
waypointNote: Waypoints hold both the hairpin (start) and the Blue Lake trailhead (descent / alternate start), both typed Trailhead; consistent with the prose, no change suggested.

road.seasonalGate: Vehicle gate at Canyon Creek bridge is a standing closure, not seasonal, pending any Forest Service repair
